import sys, os, re, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403

import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())

DOC = "PCR-009"
UO = "virus_filtration"
UO_TITLE = "Small-Virus Retentive Filtration (Step 9)"

# --- formatting: one format per kind of value, a true minus sign -------------------------------
def _mn(s):
    if s.startswith("-"):
        return ("−" + s[1:]) if any(ch in "123456789" for ch in s) else s[1:]
    return s
def fx(v, nd=2):
    return _mn(f"{float(v):,.{nd}f}")
_ALPHA_P = float(THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"])
def _p3(p):
    """Three decimals, or four where three would put the value on the wrong side of alpha or on it."""
    s3 = f"{p:.3f}"
    return f"{p:.4f}" if (float(s3) < _ALPHA_P) != (p < _ALPHA_P) or float(s3) == _ALPHA_P else s3
def pv(p):
    """A p-value in running text."""
    return "p < 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {_p3(p)}"
def pn(p):
    """A p-value in a table cell."""
    return "< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else _p3(p)
def floor2(x):
    """Two decimals rounded down, for a lower bound stated as "p ≥"."""
    import math
    return f"{math.floor(x * 100) / 100:.2f}"
def inward(x, up, sig=3):
    """A range edge rounded to three significant figures toward the inside of the range, as the
    PAR table of doe_report prints it."""
    import math
    x = float(x)
    step = 10 ** (math.floor(math.log10(abs(x))) - sig + 1)
    q = x / step
    if abs(q - round(q)) < 1e-9:
        return round(round(q) * step, 12)
    return round((math.ceil(q) if up else math.floor(q)) * step, 12)
rng_s = lambda r: f"{r[0]:g}–{r[1]:g}"
NEAR_AICC = 2.0                    # models within this many AICc units are near-equivalent (REPORT-LESSONS)

assert T.nor_change(PV) is None and T.nor_change(PP) is None        # no NOR changed at Version 2.0

def crossing(predict_fn, claim, lo=RNG_V[0], hi=RNG_V[1], n=90001):
    xs = np.linspace(lo, hi, n)
    y = predict_fn(xs)
    ok = y >= claim
    if ok.all():
        return None
    i = int(np.argmax(~ok))
    return float(np.interp(claim, [y[i], y[i - 1]], [xs[i], xs[i - 1]]))
CROSS_V = crossing(lambda xs: D.predict(UO, "mvm_lrf", natural={"filtration_volume": xs}), CL_M)
assert CROSS_V is not None and NOR_V[1] < CROSS_V < RNG_V[1]
MEAS_BELOW = [(k, int(r.run), r.filtration_volume, r.pressure, r.mvm_lrf)
              for k, d in (("screening", SCR), ("response-surface", RSM)) for _, r in d.iterrows() if r.mvm_lrf < CL_M]

F_MEAN, F_SD = float(FF["model"].params["const"]), float(FF["rmse"])

# --- deletion of runs: the flagged runs of criterion 4, and every run in turn -----------------------
def _coded(nat):
    return pd.DataFrame({"coded_" + f: np.atleast_1d(D.to_coded(UO, f, np.asarray(nat[f], float))) for f in FAC})
def _pred(sel, nat, alpha=0.05):
    sf = sel["model"].get_prediction(ad.matrix(_coded(nat), sel["terms"], False)).summary_frame(alpha=alpha)
    b = np.exp if sel["scale"] == "log" else (lambda v: v)
    return b(sf["mean"].to_numpy()), b(sf["obs_ci_lower"].to_numpy()), b(sf["obs_ci_upper"].to_numpy())
NORG = pd.DataFrame(list(itertools.product(*[[uo.param(f).nor[0], uo.param(f).setpoint, uo.param(f).nor[1]] for f in FAC])),
                    columns=FAC)
GRID11 = pd.DataFrame(list(itertools.product(*[D.to_natural(UO, f, np.linspace(-1, 1, 11)) for f in FAC])), columns=FAC)
def _contig(xs, mask, centre):
    i = int(np.argmin(np.abs(xs - centre)))
    if not mask[i]:
        return None
    lo = hi = i
    while lo > 0 and mask[lo - 1]:
        lo -= 1
    while hi < len(xs) - 1 and mask[hi + 1]:
        hi += 1
    return float(xs[lo]), float(xs[hi])
def deletion(resp, drop):
    d = D0 if drop is None else D0[D0["run"] != drop].reset_index(drop=True)
    sel = ad.select_model(d, resp, FAC, TH)
    assert not sel["exact"]
    out = {"run": drop, "n": len(d), "terms": list(sel["terms"]), "adequate": bool(sel["adequate"]),
           "scale": sel["scale"], "gap": sel["gap"], "sel": sel}
    if resp == "mvm_lrf":
        m, _, _ = _pred(sel, {f: NORG[f].to_numpy() for f in FAC})
        out["worst"] = float(m.min())
        out["nor_met"] = bool(out["worst"] >= CL_M) if sel["adequate"] else None
        xs = np.linspace(RNG_V[0], RNG_V[1], D.PAR_GRID)
        worst = np.array([_pred(sel, {"filtration_volume": np.full(3, x),
                                      "pressure": np.array([NOR_P[0], SP_P, NOR_P[1]])})[0].min() for x in xs])
        out["par_v"] = _contig(xs, worst >= CL_M, SP_V)
        g = _pred(sel, {f: GRID11[f].to_numpy() for f in FAC})[0]
        out["ds_frac"] = float(np.mean(g >= CL_M))         # fragments and XMuLV exclude no grid point
        out["b1"] = float(sel["model"].params.get("filtration_volume", np.nan))
    else:
        m, lo, hi = _pred(sel, {f: NORG[f].to_numpy() for f in FAC})
        out["pi_lo"], out["pi_hi"] = float(lo.min()), float(hi.max())
        meas = np.concatenate([SCR[resp].to_numpy(float), d[resp].to_numpy(float)])
        out["meas_met"] = bool(np.all(meas <= CR_F))
        out["nor_met"] = bool(out["pi_hi"] <= CR_F and out["pi_lo"] >= 0) if sel["adequate"] else out["meas_met"]
    return out
RUNS = [int(x) for x in RSM["run"]]
LOO = {r: deletion("mvm_lrf", r) for r in [None] + RUNS}
LOOF = {r: deletion("lmw_cesds_pct", r) for r in [None] + RUNS}
D_ALL, D5, D2 = LOO[None], LOO[5], LOO[2]

assert CURV_SCR["lmw_cesds_pct"] < 0 < CURV_RSM_F
_cs, _cr = SCR[SCR.run_type == "center"]["lmw_cesds_pct"], RSM[RSM.run_type == "center"]["lmw_cesds_pct"]
_fs, _fr = SCR[SCR.run_type == "factorial"]["lmw_cesds_pct"], RSM[RSM.run_type == "factorial"]["lmw_cesds_pct"]

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

This report presents the Stage 1 process characterization of the small virus retentive filtration step (Step 9) of the A-Mab drug substance process. The step removes virus by size. It is the dedicated small virus removal operation of the purification train and the principal source of clearance of minute virus of mice (MVM), and it also carries a claim for xenotropic murine leukemia virus (XMuLV). The study followed the characterization plan PCP-009 and supports the transfer of the process from Cambridge, MA, to Grafton, WI, under PTP-001. It was run on a scale-down model of the commercial step in two designed experiments in filtration volume (load) and filtration pressure, a screening design of `{python} n_scr` runs and a face-centred central composite design of `{python} n_rsm` runs. Version 2.0 judges each output against the intermediate acceptance criteria of the master plan PCMP-001 Version 2.0. It analyses each response-surface output with the model that a model selection chose, in place of the full quadratic of the plan (@sec-changes).

Filtration volume was the only parameter with a detected effect. Across the range studied, from `{python} f"{RNG_V[0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{RNG_V[1]:g}"` L/m2, the mean MVM log reduction factor (LRF) fell by `{python} fx(-EFF_V)` log10 along a straight line. No term containing filtration pressure was significant for any output. The selected model of MVM LRF passes the model F-test of PCMP-001 §7.2, shows no lack of fit, and meets the limit on overfitting, which allows predicted R² to fall short of R² by at most `{python} fx(GAPMAX)`. It fails the criterion on residuals and influential runs, because one run moves the fit more than that criterion allows. Its Cook's distance is above the median of the F distribution. That run, run 5, is the run at `{python} f"{RUN5.filtration_volume:g}"` L/m2 and `{python} f"{RUN5.pressure:g}"` psi, with the highest LRF of the runs at that volume. XMuLV LRF has no adequate model and is judged on its measured results. Fragments and step yield did not depend on either parameter.

Each output with a criterion met its intermediate acceptance criterion across the normal operating range (NOR). The least favourable NOR combination is the combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the two parameters that gives the lowest predicted LRF. There the mean predicted MVM LRF is `{python} fx(M_NORHI)` log10, against the LRF claimed for this step, `{python} fx(CL_M)` log10. Every measured XMuLV LRF, from `{python} fx(MEAS_X.min())` to `{python} fx(MEAS_X.max())` log10, met its claim of `{python} fx(CL_X)` log10, and XMuLV LRF has no PAR. For fragments the upper 95 % limit of a single run within the NOR is `{python} fx(F_PI_HI)` %, against the criterion of `{python} fx(CR_F)` %. The proven acceptable range (PAR) of filtration volume for MVM is `{python} PAR_V_N` L/m2 in the NOR-propagated analysis, in which the claim must hold with filtration pressure anywhere in its NOR. It extends `{python} f"{MARG_V:g}"` L/m2 beyond the upper NOR edge. The PAR of filtration pressure for MVM is the whole range studied. The design space covers `{python} fx(DS_PCT, 0)` % of the characterized region on the grid evaluated, and only filtration volumes above `{python} fx(CROSS_V, 1)` L/m2 lie outside it. With run 5 deleted, the PAR of filtration volume and the design space would both reach the end of the range studied, while the judgement over the NOR and the terms of the selected model would not change.

Both parameters were classified as well-controlled critical process parameters (WC-CPP). Filtration volume lowers the MVM LRF by `{python} fx(-EFF_V)` log10 across its range, and its PAR extends `{python} f"{MARG_V:g}"` L/m2 beyond its NOR. No effect of filtration pressure was detected, and its class follows the A-Mab case study and the scope of the viral clearance claim (@sec-classification). The integrated model of the train gives a process capability index (Cpk) of `{python} fx(CPK_M)` for the cumulative MVM clearance of the drug substance and of `{python} fx(CPK_X)` for XMuLV, both above the target of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` and the minimum of `{python} f"{CPK_MIN:.1f}"` of PCMP-001. No simulated batch fell below either cumulative requirement.

Two study events were recorded, a transient pressure excursion to `{python} dev_009_01_pmax_psi` psi and a membrane lot whose flux was `{python} dev_009_02_flux_deficit_pct` % below the value typical for the vendor. Every run concerned was retained in the analysis, as Version 1.0 recorded, and the record does not name the runs. The register of discrepancies holds `{python} N_PD` discrepancies from the plan (@sec-discrepancies). Two concern the analysis, the model selection (PD-009-01) and the use of a model that does not meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs for the ranges and the design space (PD-009-02). Four record results and comparisons that PCP-009 required and the record does not hold (PD-009-03 to PD-009-06), among them the flux decay and the integrity tests of the qualification runs and the integrity tests and virus controls of the design runs. The last records the analyses that the plan does not contain, among them the deletion of every response-surface run in turn, a test of the curvature of the two designs against each other and the capability analysis (PD-009-07). The results of this report roll up into the master report PCMR-001, which consolidates the cumulative viral clearance claim.

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

## Product and unit operation {#sec-product}

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose principal mechanism of action is antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) [@amab2009]. It is purified by the platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, small virus retentive filtration and ultrafiltration / diafiltration. The commercial process runs at a production bioreactor scale of `{python} f"{SCALE_L:,}"` L.

The small virus retentive filtration step filters the flow-through pool of anion exchange through a membrane whose pore size distribution retains the parvoviruses while the antibody passes. The step is run at a set filtration pressure, in psi, up to a set filtration volume, which is the volume of load filtered per square metre of membrane, in L/m2. MVM, a parvovirus, is among the smallest viruses of concern, and this step is the principal source of its clearance. XMuLV, an enveloped retrovirus, is many times larger than the pores. The clearance of the step is orthogonal to that of low-pH viral inactivation (Step 6) and anion exchange chromatography (Step 8), because it removes virus by size and not by inactivation or by binding [@ichq5a].

The step forms no quality attribute. It contributes a log reduction to the two cumulative viral clearance requirements of the drug substance. Its filtrate is also judged against the drug substance criterion for fragments, because no later step changes them (@sec-par). Step yield is a process performance output with no criterion.

The plan paired with this report is PCP-009. @tbl-related lists the documents to which this report relates.

## Objectives {#sec-objectives}

The objectives of the study were those of PCP-009 §2.

1. Qualify a scale-down model of the step, and show that it represents the commercial step for virus retention, for flux decay and for step yield.
2. Determine which of the parameters affect the two viral clearance responses and the step yield, in what direction and by how much.
3. Fit a response-surface model for each response over the characterization ranges, and establish whether it predicts the mean response adequately.
4. Derive a proven acceptable range for each parameter against each of the two viral clearance responses.
5. Classify each parameter under SOP-4001 and define what the step contributes to the control strategy and to the modular viral clearance claim.

Version 2.0 of the plan adds fragments to objectives 2 to 4. The screening design identifies the parameters that have an effect. The response-surface model is the predictive model, and every range in this report comes from it. @sec-conclusions states the outcome against each objective.

## Regulatory and scientific basis {#sec-regulatory}

The study belongs to Stage 1, process design, of the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced approach of ICH Q8(R2) and ICH Q11. Prior knowledge and risk assessment identify the parameters that may affect quality, and designed experiments then measure and bound their effects [@ichq8; @ichq11]. Criticality is treated as a continuum, as ICH Q8(R2) describes it, and the risk assessment that scoped the study followed ICH Q9(R1) [@ichq8; @ichq9]. Viral clearance is evaluated under ICH Q5A(R2). Each step that clears virus is studied in its own spiking model, and its log reduction enters the cumulative claim as a module [@ichq5a]. The process model, the attribute framework and the risk method follow the A-Mab case study [@amab2009].

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Platform and prior-product knowledge {#sec-platform}

The small virus retentive filtration step has been used to manufacture three earlier licensed humanized IgG1 antibodies of the platform, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and to supply A-Mab clinical material, with the same filter type and the same mode of operation [@amab2009]. Their history gives the platform claim of the step, `{python} fx(CL_M)` log10 for each of the two model viruses (PCMP-001 §7.4). The mechanism of removal is size exclusion and does not depend on the antibody, so the platform experience gives the expected direction of each effect. How the anion exchange pool of A-Mab fouls the membrane is specific to the product, and the effects were therefore measured on A-Mab material.

MVM sits close to the pore size cut-off of the membrane. Its retention depends on the fraction of pores at the large end of the distribution and on the flow through them. As the membrane fouls with product and residual impurity, the flux shifts toward the least fouled and largest pores, and small virus can pass. MVM retention is therefore expected to fall as the volume filtered per unit area rises, so the claim is most at risk at the maximum load. PCP-009 §6.3 also expected the fall to accelerate toward the top of the volume range, as the shift of flux to the largest pores progresses.

A higher filtration pressure raises the flux. It also compacts the fouling layer, which raises the resistance of that layer, but the flux still rises with pressure. PCP-009 expected MVM retention to fall at high pressure as more filtrate passes the largest open pores. A low pressure or an interruption of flow lets virus held in the pore structure diffuse through. For this reason the claim of the step is made over a pressure range and for uninterrupted filtration. PCP-009 §4.3 reasoned that the load decides how much of the membrane is still open and the pressure how fast the filtrate crosses what is left. On that reasoning the plan expected the fall of MVM retention with load to be steeper at high pressure than at low pressure.

XMuLV is many times larger than the pores. It is retained while the membrane is intact, so its clearance is expected not to depend on either parameter. The antibody passes the pores freely, so step yield loses only the product held up in the system and in the fouling layer on the membrane. The hold-up of the system is fixed, so it is a smaller share of a larger load and on its own would raise the yield as the load rises. The fouling layer, and the product held in it, grow with the volume filtered and lower the yield. PCP-009 expected yield to be high and to fall slowly as the load rises. That holds only if the loss in the fouling layer grows faster than the share of the fixed hold-up falls. Fragments, the clipped species of the antibody, are smaller than the intact antibody and pass the pores in the same way, so the step is not expected to change the fragment level of its load.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqa}

The step contributes log reduction to the two viral safety attributes of @tbl-cqa and is judged against the criterion for fragments. The acceptance values of the two viral safety attributes are cumulative requirements on the drug substance. They are met by the claims of several steps together and cannot be applied to one step. PCMP-001 §3 takes both requirements from the A-Mab case study. There they are the total log reductions of the platform train, low-pH treatment, anion exchange and small virus retentive filtration together, for A-Mab and three other antibodies [@amab2009, p. 165]. For XMuLV the case study checks that total against the retrovirus-like particles per dose estimated by electron microscopy [@amab2009, p. 166]. It gives this check for XMuLV only.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cq = cqas_by_keys(["lrv_mvm", "lrv_xmulv", "fragments_lmw"])[["Category", "CQA", "Acceptance", "Criticality", "Tool #1"]].copy()
_cq["Tool #1"] = _cq["Tool #1"].astype(int).astype(str)
T.frame(_cq, "Quality attributes to which the step contributes, with their drug substance criteria and criticality.",
        "tbl-cqa", merge=["Category"], align=["l", "P{4.6cm}", "P{3.6cm}", "l", "r"],
        notes=[("", "VH, very high. L, low. Tool #1 is the criticality score of the A-Mab case study, the product "
                    "of impact and uncertainty.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Both viral safety attributes are of very high criticality. It was assigned by rule, because a viral contamination would harm the patient directly (PCMP-001 §3). MVM is the virus whose retention the operating parameters of this step can degrade. Low-pH viral inactivation makes no claim for MVM, because a parvovirus has no lipid envelope for low pH to disrupt. The cumulative MVM requirement of `{python} f"{REQ_M:g}"` log10 therefore rests on the claims of anion exchange and of this step alone (PCMP-001 §7.4).

Fragments are of low criticality. They form in culture and during the harvest hold, where proteases released from lysed cells clip the antibody, and the CQA register assigns them to harvest. The A-Mab case study lists fragmentation among the typical quality attributes of an antibody, but its table of the basis for acceptable ranges gives fragments no limit [@amab2009, pp. 30, 56]. The sponsor set the criterion of `{python} fx(CR_F)` % when fragments joined the CQA register at Version 2.0 (PCMP-001 §3).

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection {#sec-risk}

The risk assessment RA-001 ranked every parameter of the train twice, for its potential impact on the quality attributes and for its potential to interact with other parameters [@ichq9]. Parameters ranked high on either ranking were assigned to multivariate study, and parameters ranked lower to univariate study. For this step RA-001 assigned its `{python} N_PAR` parameters to multivariate study and none to univariate study. Filtration volume was ranked high because fouling shifts the flow to the larger pores as the volume filtered per unit area rises, so MVM retention falls. Filtration pressure was ranked high because a loss of pressure or a stop of flow lets MVM held in the pore structure diffuse into the filtrate, and because a higher pressure drives more filtrate through the pores that remain open. No parameter of the step was left out of the study on prior knowledge alone, because a viral safety claim is supported by product specific data even where the mechanism is well understood.

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The scale-down model uses the same filter type as manufacturing, and the load is scaled by membrane area (PCMP-001 §5). The volumetric load in L/m2 and the filtration pressure of the model therefore correspond to the commercial step.

The qualification runs were made in study S-VF-SDM, from `{python} W_SDM[0]` to `{python} W_SDM[1]`, under the scale-down model procedure SOP-1001 and before the screening runs began. The study compared `{python} OFF_Y['n_sd']` scale-down runs at the set-points with `{python} OFF_Y['n_m']` manufacturing-scale batches. PCP-009 §5.1 named three outputs for this comparison, the flux decay profile, the step yield and the post-use integrity test result, and required the load material, the filtration temperature and the hold-up volume per area to be matched. The record holds step yield alone. The flux decay profile and the post-use integrity test results are not recorded for either scale, and neither is the matching (PD-009-03). Version 1.0 of this report stated that every run passed its post-use integrity test, but no result of the test is recorded, for these runs or for the design runs (@sec-operation). The comparison therefore rests on step yield alone.

The model is qualified by the offset rule of PCMP-001 §7.1. The offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs at the set-points minus the mean of the manufacturing batches, with its two-sided `{python} f"{OFF_CI:g}"` % confidence interval. The model is qualified for an output when the conclusion against its criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of that interval. Step yield has no criterion at this step, so its offset is recorded and no conclusion depends on it (@tbl-sdm-offsets). The mean step yield was `{python} fx(100*OFF_Y['mean_sd'], 1)` % at scale-down and `{python} fx(100*OFF_Y['mean_m'], 1)` % at manufacturing scale, an offset of `{python} fx(100*OFF_Y['offset'], 1)` percentage points with a `{python} f"{OFF_CI:g}"` % confidence interval of `{python} fx(100*OFF_Y['lo'], 1)` to `{python} fx(100*OFF_Y['hi'], 1)` points.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets(["virus_filtration"]).show()
```

The two LRF and fragments were not compared at the two scales. Their offset is unknown, not zero, and they are judged as the scale-down model gives them (PCMP-001 §7.1). Virus cannot be spiked into a manufacturing batch, so every clearance figure of this report comes from the scale-down model, and its representativeness rests on the spiking model [@ichq5a]. The representativeness of the fragment results rests on the mechanism of the step (@sec-platform). No output with a criterion therefore has a measured offset, and the judgements of MVM LRF, XMuLV LRF and fragments are made on the scale-down results under these assumptions.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

PCP-009 §5.2 specifies the flow-through pool of anion exchange as the load of every run, and the record does not identify the pool used in each run (PD-009-06). Each design point was run once, at the filtration pressure of the point and up to its filtration volume (Appendices A and B). Both model viruses were spiked into the load of every run, and every run gave an MVM LRF and an XMuLV LRF. The order of execution of each run is recorded and enters the residual tests (@sec-statistics). The designs varied the two parameters of @tbl-params. The other operating variables of the step are set by the operation procedure SOP-2012 and were not factors of the designs.

PCP-009 §5.2 planned the step yield of each design run from the same spiked run, by protein mass balance from the ultraviolet absorbance of the load and of the pooled filtrate. PCP-009 §5.4 asked instead for an unspiked load and an unspiked filtrate pool to be assayed for the yield, which cannot exist when every design run is spiked, so the plan conflicts with itself. The record gives the yield of each spiked run as a single value. It holds no protein concentration, no volume, no named assay and no sample of the load taken before spiking (PD-009-05).

PCP-009 §5.2 required the filter of each run to be integrity tested before and after the run under SOP-2012, and a run whose post-use test failed to be excluded. No integrity test result is recorded for any design run (PD-009-04), and no run was excluded. The claim made from these runs applies to uninterrupted filtration, and no run of the record is described as interrupted.

## Analytical methods {#sec-analytical}

The methods of @tbl-sops measured the outputs. MVM was titred by TCID50 with qPCR confirmation (AMV-3018), XMuLV by TCID50 (AMV-3017) and fragments by nrCE-SDS (AMV-3020). The LRF of a run is the base-ten logarithm of the total virus in the spiked load divided by the total virus in the filtrate (PCP-009 §5.3). PCP-009 §5.2 names ultraviolet absorbance for the step yield, and the record names no assay (@sec-operation). Appendix D summarises the methods.

The record holds one LRF per run for each virus. It does not hold the titres of the spiked load and the filtrate, the limit of detection reached, or the results of the cytotoxicity, interference and spike recovery controls that PCP-009 §5.3 required. Nor does it hold the achieved titre of each run, the clarification of the virus stock or the identification of each sample by run and volumetric load (PCP-009 §5.4 and §12). Every LRF in the record is a point value. Whether any filtrate titre was below the limit of detection, which would make its LRF a lower bound, cannot be read from the record.

Both designs ran after the method decision AMD-001, so fragments were measured by nrCE-SDS on every run of both designs (@tbl-methods-by-study). The method has a limit of quantitation of `{python} f"{CESDS_LOQ:g}"` % and an absolute standard deviation of `{python} fx(CESDS_SD)` percentage points. Aggregate was not measured at this step.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

PCP-009 §5.4 planned samples of the load before spiking, of the spiked load and of the filtrate, with the filtrate sampled as sequential fractions across the volumetric load and as a pool. The record holds one result per run for each output, no result for a fraction and not the volume actually filtered in each run (@sec-discrepancies). The log reduction therefore cannot be resolved against the volume filtered within a run, and the effect of filtration volume is estimated between runs only. The screening design had `{python} n_scr_c` replicates of the centre point, and the response-surface design had `{python} n_rsm_c`. Their spread gives the pure error of each design for the lack of fit tests.

## Statistical methods {#sec-statistics}

Both factors were coded to −1 and +1 at the ends of the range studied and to 0 at its midpoint, so that coefficients are comparable between the two factors and between the two designs. A coded coefficient is the change in the response over half the range studied, `{python} f"{HALF_V:g}"` L/m2 for filtration volume and `{python} f"{HALF_P:g}"` psi for filtration pressure. Terms significant at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` were treated as real (PCMP-001 §6.2). In this report the terms of a model are counted without the intercept.

The screening design was analysed by ordinary least squares with both main effects and their interaction. An effect is twice the coded coefficient, which is the change in the response across the whole range studied, as PCMP-001 §6.2 states it. PCP-009 §5.5 states effects as the change over half the range, which is the coefficient, and Appendix C gives both. The screening model identifies effects. Its centre points test for curvature through the one degree of freedom left for lack of fit, but they cannot attribute the curvature to a factor.

Each response-surface output was analysed by model selection, the analysis that INV-002 adopted as corrective action CA3. It replaced the full quadratic model of PCP-009 §5.5 (@sec-discrepancies). The selection has three steps.

1. The scale. The Box-Cox profile of the full quadratic gives the power of the response that best suits a least squares fit, with its 95 % interval [@boxcox1964]. The log scale is used where that interval contains 0 and excludes 1, and the raw scale otherwise. Every interval at this step contained both 0 and 1, so every output was modelled on the raw scale.
2. The terms. The full quadratic in two factors has `{python} N_FULL` terms, the two main effects, their interaction and the two squares. It has `{python} N_CAND` hierarchical submodels, counting the intercept-only model, in which an interaction appears only with both of its main effects and a square only with its main effect. Every submodel was fitted, and the one with the lowest AICc was selected. AICc estimates how well a model would predict new runs and penalises every estimated term. Its small-sample correction raises the penalty when the runs are few for the number of terms, as in these designs [@hurvich1989; @burnham2002]. The residual variance is counted as a parameter of the model. A stepwise search changes one term at a time and can stop where only a combination of changes would lower AICc further. On these data a stepwise search in either direction would have stopped at the same model for every output with a criterion.
3. The check. The selected model was judged against the four criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 below. An intercept-only model states that the output does not depend on the parameters within the range studied. An output with no adequate model is judged on its measured results and sets no range.

PCP-009 §7 states the four adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 with their thresholds.

1. A significant model. The model F-test is significant at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"`. An intercept-only model has no F-test, and the criterion does not apply to it.
2. No significant lack of fit. The lack of fit test against the pure error of the centre points is not significant at α = `{python} f"{LOF_ALPHA:g}"`.
3. The limit on overfitting. Predicted R², calculated from the prediction error sum of squares, falls short of R² by no more than `{python} fx(GAPMAX)` [@montgomery2017].
4. Residuals and influence. The absolute residuals regressed on the predicted values, and the residuals regressed on the order of execution, show no slope significant at α = `{python} f"{RES_ALPHA:g}"`. A run with a Cook's distance above `{python} f"{COOK_K:g}"`/n is examined by deleting it and repeating the judgement. The model fails the criterion only where a run's Cook's distance exceeds the median of the F distribution with p and n − p degrees of freedom, where p is the number of model parameters including the intercept and n the number of runs.

R², adjusted R² and predicted R² are reported for every model. PCP-009 §7 also keeps the Version 1.0 conditions that the residuals show no material departure from normality and that the residual standard error is small against the distance between the predicted response and its criterion, and it leaves the judgement of both to this report. Normality is judged on the normal quantile plot and by the Shapiro-Wilk test at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"`. The residual standard error is judged small against that distance when the end of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run on the side of the criterion still meets the criterion at the least favourable NOR combination. Several analyses of this report are not in PCP-009 (PD-009-07). They are the deletion of every response-surface run, the test of the curvature of the two designs against each other, the Shapiro-Wilk test and the reading of the two Version 1.0 conditions by the prediction interval of a single run, the comparisons with the models within `{python} f"{NEAR_AICC:g}"` AICc units of the selected one and with stepwise searches, and the capability analysis.

Each output with a criterion was judged at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the two parameters, `{python} len(NORG)` combinations in all. Viral clearance was judged on the mean predicted LRF at the least favourable of these combinations, because viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions (PCMP-001 §6.4). The lower end of the two-sided 95 % prediction interval of a single run there is given for information. Fragments were judged on the exact 95 % prediction interval of a single run at each combination, which includes the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients and the residual. The interval is two-sided, so its upper end is a one-sided `{python} f"{PCT_UP:g}"` % limit. An output with no adequate model was judged on every measured result of both designs. No offset was applied, because no output with a criterion has a measured offset at this step (@sec-sdm). @sec-par defines the two PAR analyses, and @sec-design-space the grid on which the design space was evaluated.

Capability was estimated from the integrated model of the train (PCMP-001 §6.5) and judged against the target and the minimum of PCMP-001 §7.9. The analyses followed the design of experiments procedure SOP-1002. The Monte-Carlo analyses use a fixed random seed, so every number of this report can be regenerated from the data.

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space {#sec-factors}

@tbl-params gives the two parameters of the step with their set-points, their NOR and the ranges studied. Both parameters were factors of both designs. The NOR and the set-points were not changed at Version 2.0, so the NOR in force is the NOR as characterized.

                    [LET["pressure"], NM_P, U_P, f"{SP_P:g}", rng_s(NOR_P), rng_s(RNG_P)]],
                   columns=["Code", "Parameter", "Unit", "Set-point", "NOR", "Range studied"])

The range of filtration volume runs from the lower NOR edge, `{python} f"{RNG_V[0]:g}"` L/m2, to `{python} f"{RNG_V[1]:g}"` L/m2, above the upper NOR edge of `{python} f"{NOR_V[1]:g}"` L/m2. It was widened upward only, because MVM retention was expected to fall as the load rises, so that the edge of acceptable performance would lie above the NOR. The pressure range of `{python} rng_s(RNG_P)` psi extends beyond the NOR of `{python} rng_s(NOR_P)` psi on both sides. Low pressures were included because a low pressure was expected to let retained virus diffuse through, and high pressures because they drive more filtrate through the largest open pores. The ranges studied form the knowledge space of the step, and no claim in this report extends beyond them.

The studies of the step ran one after the other (@tbl-windows). Each window runs from the first to the last day of runs of its study, and all of them closed before Version 1.0 of this report was approved on `{python} REP_V1`. The record names no instrumented system under calibration and change control for these studies (PCMP-001 Table 5.1), so no calibration status is given.

## Screening design {#sec-screening-design}

The screening study S-VF-DOE was a two-level full factorial in both factors with centre points, `{python} n_scr` runs in all, of which `{python} n_scr_f` were the factorial runs at the corners of the ranges studied and `{python} n_scr_c` were replicates of the centre point (Appendix A). With two factors the full factorial estimates both main effects and their interaction free of aliasing. The interaction model fits four parameters to `{python} N_SCR_PTS` distinct design points, the corners and the centre, so its fit statistics overstate how well it fits (PCMP-001 §6.2). The one degree of freedom left for lack of fit tests for curvature.

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm-design}

The response-surface study S-VF-RSM was a face-centred central composite design in both factors, `{python} n_rsm` runs in all, made up of `{python} n_rsm_f` factorial runs, `{python} n_rsm_a` axial runs and `{python} n_rsm_c` replicates of the centre point (Appendix B). The axial runs sit on the edges of the ranges studied, because settings outside those ranges are not settings for which the step may be claimed. The design supports the full quadratic model in both factors. Its centre points give the pure error for the lack of fit test, with `{python} n_rsm_c - 1` degrees of freedom.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

No parameter of this step was assigned to univariate study. PCP-009 §6.4 allowed a univariate confirmation run where the designs could not separate an effect, and none was made.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility {#sec-centre}

@tbl-centre gives the centre-point results of both designs. In the response-surface design the SD of the four centre points was `{python} fx(CEN[('rsm','mvm_lrf')][2])` log10 for MVM LRF and `{python} fx(CEN[('rsm','xmulv_lrf')][2])` log10 for XMuLV LRF. The three MVM centre points of the screening design spread more widely, from `{python} fx(CEN[('screening','mvm_lrf')][3])` to `{python} fx(CEN[('screening','mvm_lrf')][4])` log10, an SD of `{python} fx(CEN[('screening','mvm_lrf')][2])` log10. The variance of the centre points of each design is its pure error, the basis of its lack of fit test.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_lab = {"mvm_lrf": "MVM LRF (log10)", "xmulv_lrf": "XMuLV LRF (log10)", "lmw_cesds_pct": "Fragments, LMW (%)",
        "step_yield": "Step yield (%)"}
_rows_cen = []
for _k, _kn in (("screening", "Screening"), ("rsm", "Response surface")):
    for _r in RESP4:
        _n, _m, _s, _lo, _hi = CEN[(_k, _r)]
        _sc = 100 if _r == "step_yield" else 1
        _rows_cen.append([_kn, _lab[_r], str(_n), fx(_m * _sc, 1 if _r == "step_yield" else 2), fx(_s * _sc), fx(100 * _s / _m, 1)])
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_rows_cen, columns=["Design", "Response", "n", "Mean", "SD", "CV (%)"]),
        "Centre-point results of the two designs.", "tbl-centre", merge=["Design"],
        align=["l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "SD and mean in the unit of the response. CV, the SD as a percentage of the mean.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

## Factor effects in the screening design {#sec-screening}

Filtration volume had the only significant effect in the screening design (@tbl-scr-effects). Raising it from `{python} f"{RNG_V[0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{RNG_V[1]:g}"` L/m2 lowered MVM LRF by `{python} fx(-E_A_M)` log10 (`{python} pv(P_A_M)`). The effect of pressure on MVM LRF (`{python} fx(E_B_M)` log10, `{python} pv(P_B_M)`) and the interaction (`{python} fx(E_AB_M)` log10, `{python} pv(P_AB_M)`) were not significant. The F-test of the whole screening model of MVM LRF gave `{python} pv(SCR_P_M)`, with `{python} SCR_DFR` residual degrees of freedom. No term was significant for XMuLV LRF, fragments or step yield.

```{python}

         for _r in RESP4]
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_rows_scrfit, columns=["Response", "R²", "Adj. R²", "Pred. R²", "Model F-test p", "Curvature p"]),
        "Screening models of the four responses.", "tbl-scr-fit", align=["l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "Curvature p, the lack of fit test of the interaction model, one degree of freedom, which compares "
                    "the centre points with the factorial runs.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

    _sc = 100 if _r == "step_yield" else 1
    for _t in ["A", "B", "AB"]:

        _rows_screff.append([f"{_lab2[_r]} ({_unit[_r]})", _t, fx(_e["Effect"] * _sc), fx(2 * _e["Std. err."] * _sc), pn(_e["p-value"])])

The centre points of the screening design showed curvature for fragments. The three centre points read `{python} fx(-CURV_SCR['lmw_cesds_pct'])` percentage points lower than the factorial runs, which is significant (`{python} pv(CURV_P['lmw_cesds_pct'])`). In the response-surface design the four centre points read `{python} fx(CURV_RSM_F)` points higher than the factorial runs, the opposite sign. The difference between the two estimates, `{python} fx(CURV_DIFF)` points, is not significant (`{python} pv(CURV_PD)`), by a t-test on the pooled SD of the centre points of both designs with `{python} CURV_DF` degrees of freedom. In size both estimates are at most `{python} fx(CURV_MAXABS)` percentage points, against a criterion of `{python} fx(CR_F)` %, and of the order of the SD of the method, `{python} fx(CESDS_SD)` points. No other response showed curvature in the screening design (p ≥ `{python} MIN_OTHER_CURV_S`). The screening results identify the effects, and the response-surface design gives the predictive model.

## Response-surface models {#sec-rsm}

@tbl-reeval-virus-filtration compares the full quadratic model that PCP-009 planned, fitted to the `{python} n_rsm` planned runs, with the model each output now uses. The full quadratic did not meet the limit on overfitting for any output with a criterion. Its R² exceeded its predicted R² by `{python} fx(GAP_FULL_M)` for MVM LRF and by more for XMuLV LRF and fragments. Its adjusted R² was `{python} fx(PF_ADJ['mvm_lrf'])` for MVM LRF, `{python} fx(PF_ADJ['xmulv_lrf'])` for XMuLV LRF and `{python} fx(PF_ADJ['lmw_cesds_pct'])` for fragments. INV-002 named a refit as the remedy for each of them. Viral clearance is not a drug substance test, so no further run was spiked with virus, and fragments had no effect to resolve. The step was therefore not augmented.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.model_reevaluation("virus_filtration").show()
```

The model selection gave a straight line in filtration volume for MVM LRF, a model in pressure alone for XMuLV LRF, and an intercept-only model for fragments and for step yield. @tbl-adequacy judges each selected model against the model F-test, the lack of fit test and the limit on overfitting of PCMP-001 §7.2, and @tbl-influence against the criterion on residuals and influential runs.

MVM LRF is modelled by a straight line in filtration volume (@tbl-coef-mvm). The Box-Cox interval of λ contains both 0 and 1, so the raw scale was kept. On the grid of the selection the interval runs from the lower end of the grid, `{python} fx(BC_M['lo'])`, to `{python} fx(BC_M['hi'])`. On a grid of λ from `{python} fx(BC_GRID[0], 0)` to `{python} fx(BC_GRID[1], 0)` it runs from `{python} fx(BC_WIDE['lo'])` to `{python} fx(BC_WIDE['hi'])`. The intercept, `{python} fx(B0)` log10, is the mean predicted LRF at the midpoint of the volume range, `{python} f"{RNG_V[0] + HALF_V:g}"` L/m2. The coefficient of filtration volume is `{python} fx(B1, 3)` log10 per coded unit, with a standard error of `{python} fx(SE_B1, 3)`. Across the range studied the mean LRF therefore falls by `{python} fx(-EFF_V)` log10, which is `{python} fx(-SLOPE_PER)` log10 for every `{python} SLOPE_STEP` L/m2. The model F-test is significant (`{python} pv(FM['p'])`), the lack of fit is not (`{python} pv(FM['p_lof'])`, @tbl-anova-mvm), and R² exceeds predicted R² by `{python} fx(FM['gap'])`. The model therefore passes the F-test, shows no lack of fit and meets the limit on overfitting. The residual SD of the model is `{python} fx(FM['rmse'])` log10, against an SD of the centre points of `{python} fx(SD_PE_M)` log10. The residuals show no departure from normality (Shapiro-Wilk `{python} pv(SW['mvm_lrf'])`, @fig-diag-mvm). The next model by AICc adds the main effect of pressure and lies `{python} fx(NEXT_M_D, 1)` units higher, so no other model is within `{python} f"{NEAR_AICC:g}"` units of the selected one.

The model of MVM LRF does not meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs. Neither residual trend is significant (`{python} pv(RIM['p_spread'])` for the absolute residuals against the predicted values and `{python} pv(RIM['p_order'])` for the residuals against the order of execution). Runs 2 and 5 have a Cook's distance above `{python} f"{COOK_K:g}"`/n = `{python} fx(COOK_K / n_rsm)`. Run 5, at `{python} fx(COOK5)`, also exceeds the median of F(p, n − p), `{python} fx(RIM['f_limit'])`, and so fails the criterion. Run 5 is an axial run at the lowest filtration volume, `{python} f"{RUN5.filtration_volume:g}"` L/m2, and the centre pressure, `{python} f"{RUN5.pressure:g}"` psi, executed `{python} ordinal(ORDER5)` of `{python} n_rsm`. Its LRF, `{python} fx(RUN5.mvm_lrf)` log10, is the highest of the `{python} len(M_AT_LO)` runs of the design at that volume. Its residual is `{python} fx(RES5)` log10, and its externally studentized residual `{python} fx(SRES5, 1)`. Its leverage, `{python} fx(H5)`, is below 2p/n = `{python} fx(LEV_LIM)`. Run 2, a factorial run at the lowest volume and the highest pressure, has a residual of `{python} fx(RES2)` log10.

Both flagged runs were deleted in turn, the model selection was repeated and MVM LRF was judged over the NOR again (@tbl-deletion). Every other run of the design was deleted in the same way, because the record does not name the runs of the two study events (@sec-events). Every deletion leaves filtration volume as the only term of the selected model and the mean predicted LRF at the least favourable NOR combination between `{python} fx(min(LOO_WORST))` and `{python} fx(max(LOO_WORST))` log10, above the claim of `{python} fx(CL_M)` log10. The deletion of run 5 flattens the line, from `{python} fx(B1, 3)` to `{python} fx(D5['b1'], 3)` log10 per coded unit, and the mean prediction then meets the claim over the whole range studied. The NOR-propagated PAR of filtration volume then reaches the end of the range studied, and so does the design space. The deletion of run 2 steepens the line to `{python} fx(D2['b1'], 3)` and moves the point at which the mean prediction crosses the claim from `{python} fx(CROSS_V, 1)` to `{python} fx(CROSS2, 1)` L/m2. With run 3 or run 7 deleted, the Box-Cox interval of the remaining runs excludes 1, so that the model is fitted on the log scale, and the deletion of run 7 also carries the PAR edge to the end of the range. Across the single deletions the upper PAR edge of filtration volume lies between `{python} f"{inward(LOO_EDGE_MIN, up=False):g}"` L/m2 and the end of the range studied. No deletion changes the judgement over the NOR, and the NOR lies `{python} f"{MARG_MIN:g}"` L/m2 or more below the edge under every deletion. The model of all runs, which gives a narrower range of volume than the model without run 5, was kept for the ranges and the design space (@sec-discrepancies).
