XMuLV LRF has no adequate model. The selected model carries pressure alone, with a coefficient of `{python} fx(XB, 3)` log10 per coded unit and a residual SD of `{python} fx(FXV['rmse'])` log10, but its F-test is not significant (`{python} pv(FXV['p'])`) and R² exceeds predicted R² by `{python} fx(FXV['gap'])`, above the limit. XMuLV LRF is therefore judged on its measured results, all `{python} len(MEAS_X)` of which, from `{python} fx(MEAS_X.min())` to `{python} fx(MEAS_X.max())` log10, met the claim of `{python} fx(CL_X)` log10. The intercept-only model lies `{python} fx(NX_D, 1)` AICc units from the selected one, shows no lack of fit and meets the limit on overfitting. It predicts a mean LRF of `{python} fx(NX_MEAN)` log10 everywhere, and the judgement over the NOR would be the same under it.

The selected model of fragments is intercept-only, with a mean of `{python} fx(F_MEAN)` % and a residual SD of `{python} fx(F_SD)` percentage points. The lack of fit is not significant (`{python} pv(FF['p_lof'])`), and the model meets the limit on overfitting with a gap of `{python} fx(FF['gap'])`. Its residuals show no departure from normality (Shapiro-Wilk `{python} pv(SW['lmw_cesds_pct'])`), and the upper 95 % limit of a single run, `{python} fx(F_PI_HI)` %, meets the criterion of `{python} fx(CR_F)` %. Both conditions kept from Version 1.0, normal residuals and a residual SD small against the distance to the criterion, are therefore met. For an intercept-only model R² is zero and predicted R² is 1 − (n/(n − 1))², so the gap, (2n − 1)/(n − 1)², is fixed by the number of runs. It is `{python} fx(GAP_NOTERM(n_rsm))` with `{python} n_rsm` runs and `{python} fx(GAP_NOTERM(n_rsm - 1))` with `{python} n_rsm - 1`. Run 9, a centre run, has a Cook's distance of `{python} fx(COOK9)`, above `{python} f"{COOK_K:g}"`/n and below the median of F(p, n − p), `{python} fx(RIF['f_limit'])`. The deletion of run 9, or of any other single run, leaves an intercept-only model on `{python} n_rsm - 1` runs, whose gap of `{python} fx(GAP_NOTERM(n_rsm - 1))` exceeds the limit on overfitting whatever the results are. Fragments would then have no adequate model and no PAR, and they would be judged on their measured results, every one of which meets the criterion. The judgement over the NOR, the range carried into the control strategy, which the PARs of MVM LRF set, and the design space do not change.

The selected model of step yield is intercept-only, with a mean of `{python} fx(100 * Y_MEAN, 1)` % and a residual SD of `{python} fx(100 * Y_SD)` percentage points. The model with filtration volume lies `{python} fx(NY_D, 1)` AICc units from it, with a coefficient of `{python} fx(100 * NY_B)` points per coded unit that is not significant (`{python} pv(NY_P)`). The residual plots of XMuLV LRF, fragments and step yield are given in Appendix C (@fig-diag-xmulv, @fig-diag-frag and @fig-diag-yield).

@fig-measured shows the measured results of both designs against filtration volume. The MVM LRF falls with volume at every pressure of the response-surface design, and at high volume the line of the model of all runs lies below the line with run 5 deleted. For XMuLV LRF and fragments no term was significant in either design.

```{python}
#| label: fig-measured
#| fig-cap: "Measured results of both designs against filtration volume, with the claim or criterion of each output and the NOR shaded. Colour gives the filtration pressure, open circles the screening runs and filled squares the response-surface runs. For MVM LRF the lines are the selected model on all runs and with run 5 deleted. For fragments the line and band are the selected model and the 95 % prediction interval of a single run. XMuLV LRF has no adequate model and no line."
_col = {RNG_P[0]: "#2a78d6", (RNG_P[0] + RNG_P[1]) / 2: "#6d6d6d", RNG_P[1]: "#c0392b"}
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10, 4.2))
_xs = np.linspace(RNG_V[0], RNG_V[1], 200)
_panels = [("mvm_lrf", "MVM LRF (log10)", CL_M, "claim"), ("xmulv_lrf", "XMuLV LRF (log10)", CL_X, "claim"),
           ("lmw_cesds_pct", "Fragments, LMW (%)", CR_F, "criterion")]
for _ax, (_r, _ylab, _lim, _ll) in zip(axs, _panels):
    _ax.axvspan(NOR_V[0], NOR_V[1], color="grey", alpha=0.12, lw=0, label="NOR")
    for _d, _off, _mkr, _dl in ((SCR, -1.5, "o", "screening"), (RSM, 1.5, "s", "response surface")):
        for _p, _cc in _col.items():
            _s = _d[_d.pressure == _p]
            _ax.scatter(_s.filtration_volume + _off, _s[_r], marker=_mkr, s=34, color=_cc,
                        facecolors="none" if _d is SCR else _cc, label=f"{_dl}, {_p:g} {U_P}")
    _ax.axhline(_lim, color="#c0392b", ls="--", lw=1.0, label=_ll)
    _ax.set_xlabel(f"{NM_V} ({U_V})", fontsize=10)
    _ax.set_ylabel(_ylab, fontsize=10)
    _ax.tick_params(labelsize=9)
_y_all = D.predict(UO, "mvm_lrf", natural={"filtration_volume": _xs})
_y_5 = _pred(D5["sel"], {"filtration_volume": _xs, "pressure": np.full(len(_xs), SP_P)})[0]
axs[0].plot(_xs, _y_all, color="#1f3b73", lw=1.4, label="model, all runs")
axs[0].plot(_xs, _y_5, color="#1f3b73", lw=1.2, ls=":", label="model, run 5 deleted")
axs[0].annotate("run 5", (RUN5.filtration_volume + 1.5, RUN5.mvm_lrf), xytext=(RUN5.filtration_volume + 16, RUN5.mvm_lrf - 0.2),
                fontsize=9, arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", lw=0.6))
_m, _l, _h = D.prediction_interval(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct", {"filtration_volume": _xs, "pressure": np.full(len(_xs), SP_P)})
axs[2].plot(_xs, _m, color="#1f3b73", lw=1.2, label="model")
axs[2].fill_between(_xs, _l, _h, color="#1f3b73", alpha=0.15, lw=0, label="95 % interval, single run")
axs[2].set_ylim(0, CR_F * 1.1)
_h1, _l1 = axs[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
fig.legend(_h1, _l1, loc="lower center", ncol=4, fontsize=9, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.0))
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.2, 1, 1])
plt.show()
```

## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mechanism}

The fall of MVM LRF with filtration volume is the effect that the mechanism of the step predicts. As the membrane fouls, the flux shifts toward the largest pores, through which the parvovirus can pass, and the shift grows with the volume filtered per unit area. The data show the effect as a fall of `{python} fx(-EFF_V)` log10 across the range studied, with a standard error of `{python} fx(2 * SE_B1)` log10.

The data do not show three other effects that PCP-009 expected from the same mechanism. First, the fall was expected to accelerate toward the top of the volume range. In the full quadratic of the planned runs the square of filtration volume is positive, `{python} fx(PF_A2, 3)` log10 per coded unit squared, which is the opposite sign, and it is not significant (`{python} pv(PF_A2_P)`). Within `{python} rng_s(RNG_V)` L/m2 the decline is consistent with a straight line, and the mechanism as PCP-009 states it does not explain the absence of the acceleration. Second, MVM retention was expected to fall at high pressure, and at low pressure through diffusion. The main effect of pressure in the full quadratic is `{python} fx(PF_B, 3)` log10 per coded unit (`{python} pv(PF_B_P)`). The square of pressure is negative, `{python} fx(PF_B2, 3)`, which would mean a lower LRF at both ends of the pressure range, the shape that the mechanism predicts, but it is not significant (`{python} pv(PF_B2_P)`) and was not selected. Third, the fall with volume was expected to be steeper at high pressure. The interaction in the full quadratic is `{python} fx(PF_AB, 3)` log10 per coded unit squared, with a standard error of `{python} fx(PF_AB_SE, 3)` (`{python} pv(PF_AB_P)`), and in the screening design `{python} fx(E_AB_M)` log10 across the range (`{python} pv(P_AB_M)`). Within the range studied no dependence of the volume effect on pressure was detected at the precision of these runs. A term that is not significant is not shown to be absent, and an effect of pressure of the size of these standard errors could exist within `{python} rng_s(RNG_P)` psi.

For operation, the MVM LRF is therefore lowest at the highest volume filtered per square metre of membrane, and the claim is most at risk there. Within the pressures studied, pressure had no detected effect on any output, and the condition of uninterrupted filtration rests on the mechanism and not on these data, because the designs did not study an interruption of flow.

The results for XMuLV LRF agree with the expectation that a virus many times larger than the pores is retained independently of the operating parameters. No term was significant in either design, and every measured LRF met the claim. Every LRF in the record is a point value, and the record does not say whether any filtrate titre was below the limit of detection (@sec-analytical), so the data do not show whether retention was complete.

Fragments did not depend on either parameter, and their level in the filtrate ranged from `{python} fx(MEAS_F.min())` to `{python} fx(MEAS_F.max())` %, against the criterion of `{python} fx(CR_F)` %. The expectation that the step does not change fragments cannot be tested on these data, because fragments were measured in the filtrate and not in the load. It rests on the size of the clipped species against the pores. Step yield did not depend on either parameter. The model with filtration volume, the next by AICc, falls with load as PCP-009 expected, but its coefficient is not significant (`{python} pv(NY_P)`). The data therefore do not show whether the loss in the fouling layer grows faster than the share of the fixed hold-up falls (@sec-platform).

# Design space {#sec-design-space}

The design space of the step is the part of the characterized region in which every output with a criterion meets it at once, each on the statistic on which it is judged (PCMP-001 §6.2). A setting lies inside it when the mean predicted MVM LRF meets its claim and both ends of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run for fragments lie within their criterion. XMuLV LRF has no adequate model and draws no boundary, because every measured result met its claim. The region was evaluated on an evenly spaced grid of `{python} GRID_N` by `{python} GRID_N` points over the characterized region, `{python} rng_s(RNG_V)` L/m2 by `{python} rng_s(RNG_P)` psi.

Of the `{python} DS_N` grid points, `{python} DS_IN` lie inside the design space, `{python} fx(DS_PCT, 0)` % of the characterized region. The points outside are those at `{python} f"{RNG_V[1]:g}"` L/m2, the top of the volume range, where the mean predicted MVM LRF falls below the claim at every pressure. Between the grid points the boundary lies at `{python} fx(CROSS_V, 1)` L/m2 at every pressure, because the selected model has no pressure term. Fragments exclude no point. Drawn on the mean prediction of fragments as well, the design space is the same, because MVM LRF is judged on its mean in both and fragments exclude no point in either.

The NOR of both parameters lies inside the design space, and the design space lies inside the characterized region, which is the knowledge space of the study. Movement within the design space is not a change from the point of view of a regulatory filing under ICH Q8(R2), but it is evaluated under the change management system of the quality system [@ichq8; @ichq10]. At the boundary itself a single run meets the claim only about half the time if the variability is symmetrical, because the boundary is drawn on the mean prediction, as PCMP-001 §6.2 sets it for viral clearance. At the least favourable NOR combination the lower end of the two-sided 95 % prediction interval of a single run, a one-sided `{python} f"{PCT_UP:g}"` % limit, is `{python} fx(M_PI_LO)` log10, above the claim. It is given for information.

Deleting run 5, the axial run at `{python} f"{RUN5.filtration_volume:g}"` L/m2 and `{python} f"{RUN5.pressure:g}"` psi, or run 7, the axial run at `{python} f"{RUN7.filtration_volume:g}"` L/m2 and `{python} f"{RUN7.pressure:g}"` psi, gives a selected model that meets the claim over the whole characterized region (@tbl-deletion). The design space is not confirmed at manufacturing scale at its edges, because virus cannot be spiked at that scale. The selected model of step yield is intercept-only, so the predicted mean yield is `{python} fx(100 * Y_MEAN, 1)` % at every setting in the design space (PCP-009 §7).

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

Each output of the step with a criterion is judged against its intermediate acceptance criterion (@tbl-iac). MVM LRF and XMuLV LRF are each held to the platform claim of this step, `{python} fx(CL_M)` log10, the log reduction that the step delivered on the platform with X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab (PCMP-001 §7.4). The claims of the steps that clear each virus are summed and checked against the cumulative requirement of the drug substance. For XMuLV the claims of low-pH viral inactivation (`{python} fx(CL_VI_X)`), anion exchange (`{python} fx(CL_AEX_X)`) and this step sum to `{python} fx(SUM_X)` log10, against a requirement of `{python} f"{REQ_X:g}"` log10. For MVM the claims of anion exchange (`{python} fx(CL_AEX_M)`) and this step sum to `{python} fx(SUM_M)` log10, against `{python} f"{REQ_M:g}"` log10. The LRF claimed for this step is therefore one of three claims for XMuLV and one of two for MVM. Each step is judged against its own claim, so a shortfall at this step is not made up by another step. Fragments carry the drug substance criterion, `{python} fx(CR_F)` %, because no later step changes them.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation(["virus_filtration"]).show()
```

The criteria of this step were derived without its data. The claims come from the platform history and the fragment criterion from the CQA register (PCMP-001 §7.3). The criteria in force equal their values derived in this way, because no verification changed them. No criterion of an earlier step rests on a platform worst case of this step, so this report has no worst case to verify. The fragment criteria of the earlier steps do assume that no later step changes fragments, and so that this step leaves its load unchanged. That assumption rests on the mechanism of the step, because the record holds fragments in the filtrate and not in the load (@sec-mechanism).

@tbl-criteria-virus-filtration gives each output against its criterion over the NOR. MVM LRF met its claim, with a mean predicted LRF of `{python} fx(M_NORHI)` log10 at the least favourable NOR combination, the upper NOR edge of filtration volume. XMuLV LRF met its claim on its measured results. Fragments met their criterion, with an upper 95 % limit of a single run of `{python} fx(F_PI_HI)` % within the NOR.

```{python}
#| output: asis
# layout only: the attribute column wraps, so that the builder's table stays above the 8 pt floor at this
# step (its notes were set at 7.8 pt); no text, note or verdict changes
_crit_t = T.criteria_results("virus_filtration")
_crit_t.align = ["P{3.0cm}", "l", "r", "r", "r", "l"]
_crit_t.show()
```

Two analyses give the PAR of each parameter for each output with a criterion and an adequate model (@tbl-par). The first scans the parameter across its range studied on a grid of `{python} D.PAR_GRID_SETPOINT` points and gives the contiguous range over which the mean prediction of the response-surface model meets the criterion. The second is the NOR-propagated analysis of PCMP-001 §6.4. It scans the parameter across the same range on a grid of `{python} D.PAR_GRID` points with the other parameter moving within its NOR. For viral clearance the other parameter is set at each grid point to its NOR low, its set-point and its NOR high, and the lowest of the three mean predicted LRF must meet the claim. For fragments, `{python} f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"` values of the other parameter are drawn at each grid point from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with an SD equal to the width of its NOR divided by `{python} f"{D.NOR_SD_DIVISOR:g}"`, clipped to the range studied. Each draw carries the model residual and the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients, and the `{python} f"{PCT_UP:g}"`th percentile of the simulated batches must not exceed the criterion. The range reported is the contiguous range that contains the set-point, and the NOR-propagated range is the one carried into the control strategy (PCP-009 §8). An output with no adequate model has no PAR, and @tbl-par marks it n.a. (PCMP-001 §7.2).

```{python}
#| output: asis
_par_t = D.par_table(UO)
_lab_resp = {LAB_M: "mvm_lrf", LAB_X: "xmulv_lrf", LAB_F: "lmw_cesds_pct"}
_par_t["Criterion"] = [T.crit(*D.effective_acceptance(UO, _lab_resp[c])) for c in _par_t["CQA"]]
T.frame(_par_t, "Proven acceptable ranges of the parameters for each output with a criterion.", "tbl-par",
        merge=["CQA", "Criterion", "Basis"], align=["P{2.6cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "l", "l", "l", "l", "l", "P{2.0cm}"],
        size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Edges rounded inward to three significant figures. Basis, selected model, the PAR comes from the "
                    "selected response-surface model. No adequate model, the output has no PAR (n.a.), and every "
                    "measured result met the claim.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The PAR of filtration volume for MVM ends inside the range studied in both analyses. It is `{python} PAR_V_S` L/m2 in the first analysis and `{python} PAR_V_N` L/m2 in the NOR-propagated analysis, as @tbl-par rounds them. The mean prediction crosses the claim at `{python} fx(CROSS_V, 1)` L/m2, which is the crossing value that PCP-009 §8 asks this report to state. Below that volume the selected model predicts a mean LRF above the claim at every pressure, because it has no pressure term. The NOR of filtration volume, `{python} rng_s(NOR_V)` L/m2, lies inside its NOR-propagated PAR, which extends `{python} f"{MARG_V:g}"` L/m2 beyond the upper NOR edge. The lower edge of the PAR is the lower end of the range studied, and no run was made below it. Across the PAR the mean predicted LRF falls from `{python} fx(M_LO)` to `{python} fx(M_EDGE)` log10. The PAR of filtration pressure for MVM is the whole range studied in both analyses, and no claim is made beyond it.

@fig-par-mvm shows the two analyses for MVM against filtration volume, with the claim drawn and the acceptable region shaded green. The two panels give nearly the same edge, because the selected model has no pressure term.

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-mvm
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range of filtration volume for MVM LRF, the first analysis (left) and the NOR-propagated analysis (right), with the claim of the step and the NOR."
fig = D.fig_par(UO, "mvm_lrf", "filtration_volume")
plt.show()
```

XMuLV LRF has no adequate model and therefore no PAR (n.a. in @tbl-par). Every measured result met the claim (@sec-rsm). The selected model of fragments is intercept-only, and its interval lies below the criterion everywhere, so both of their PARs are the whole range studied for both parameters. PCP-009 §8 planned a figure for each PAR, and only @fig-par-mvm is given.

With two parameters and no interaction term in any selected model, the PARs and the design space describe one region. The design space is the characterized region below the volume at which MVM LRF crosses its claim, and the PARs are its edges. A movement of filtration volume within its PAR keeps the step inside the design space at any pressure within `{python} rng_s(RNG_P)` psi, and a movement of pressure within its PAR does so at any volume within the PAR of volume.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

Capability at commercial scale was estimated from the integrated model of the train, which runs `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` simulated batches through every step with each process parameter drawn within its NOR (PCMP-001 §6.5). The cumulative viral clearance of a simulated batch is the sum of the clearances of the steps that clear the virus. For MVM these are anion exchange (PCR-008) and this step, and for XMuLV low-pH viral inactivation (PCR-006), anion exchange and this step. The capability of the cumulative clearance therefore depends on those steps as well as on this one.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cp = cap_for(CAPK).set_index("CQA")
_crow = []
for _k in CAPK:
    _row = CAPT.loc[_k]
    _cf = cap_for([_k]).iloc[0]
    _p = POOS.loc[_k]
    _crow.append([_row["cqa"], T.crit(_row["acc_low"], _row["acc_high"], _row["spec_type"]),
                  f"{fx(_row['mean'])} ± {fx(_row['sd'])}", fx(_row["Cpk"]),
                  f"{int(_p['n_oos'])} of {int(_p['n']):,}", fx(_p["ppm_normal"])])
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_crow, columns=["Attribute", "Criterion", "Mean ± SD", "Cpk", "Batches outside",
                                      "Normal tail\n(per million)"]),
        "Capability of the drug substance attributes to which the step contributes, from the integrated model.",
        "tbl-capability", align=["P{4.4cm}", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "Viral clearance, the cumulative log10 reduction of the drug substance against the cumulative "
                    "requirement. Normal tail, the tail probability of a normal distribution with the simulated mean "
                    "and SD.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The Cpk of the cumulative MVM clearance is `{python} fx(CPK_M)` and that of the cumulative XMuLV clearance `{python} fx(CPK_X)`, against the requirements of `{python} f"{REQ_M:g}"` and `{python} f"{REQ_X:g}"` log10 (@tbl-capability). Both are above the target of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` and the minimum of `{python} f"{CPK_MIN:.1f}"` of PCMP-001 §7.9, and MVM is the tighter of the two. The Cpk of fragments is `{python} fx(CPK_F)` against the criterion of `{python} fx(CR_F)` %, also above the target. No simulated batch fell outside any of the three criteria. With none of `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` batches outside, the one-sided `{python} f"{100 * BOUND_CONF:g}"` % upper bound of the probability out of specification is `{python} fx(P_UP, 4)` for each attribute. That bound covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the integrated process model. The tail of a normal distribution with the simulated mean and SD gives `{python} fx(PPM_M)` per million for MVM, `{python} fx(PPM_X)` per million for XMuLV and a value that rounds to zero for fragments.

Within this step, the claim is judged on the response-surface model at the least favourable NOR combination (@sec-par). The capability adds the variation of the parameters within their NOR and the clearance of the other steps. Fragments are judged per batch against their criterion and are tested at release of the drug substance.

# Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

The parameters were classified under SOP-4001. Under the rule of PCP-009 §7 a parameter affects an attribute when a term that contains the parameter is significant at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"`. The class of an affected parameter then follows from the size of its effect across its PAR and from the margin between the PAR and the NOR. Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a number for either. The class of filtration volume below is therefore a judgement on the values given.

- `{python} NM_V`, `{python} CLASS_V`. A term containing the parameter is significant for MVM LRF (`{python} pv(FM['p'])`). Across its NOR-propagated PAR, `{python} PAR_V_N` L/m2, the mean predicted MVM LRF falls by `{python} fx(M_LO - M_EDGE)` log10. MVM clearance is an attribute of very high criticality. The PAR extends `{python} f"{MARG_V:g}"` L/m2 beyond the upper NOR edge, and its lower edge is the end of the range studied. The volumetric load is set by the volume of load applied to a filter of known area, so it can be held within its NOR. The parameter was classified as a WC-CPP on this margin and this control. With run 5 deleted the PAR would reach the end of the range studied, and the class would be the same.
- `{python} NM_P`, `{python} CLASS_P`. No term containing the parameter is significant for any output, in either design (MVM LRF `{python} pv(PF_B_P)` for the main effect and `{python} pv(PF_B2_P)` for the square in the full quadratic, XMuLV LRF `{python} pv(XB_P)` in its selected model, which is not adequate). No effect of pressure on an attribute was therefore detected within `{python} rng_s(RNG_P)` psi, and the class does not follow from the rule of PCP-009 §7. The A-Mab case study classes both parameters of this step as WC-CPP, "since both are easy to control and have minimal impact on LRF when operated within their acceptable ranges" [@amab2009, p. 157]. The parameter was classified as a WC-CPP on that basis and on the scope of the viral clearance claim, which holds only for the pressures of the spiking runs, `{python} rng_s(RNG_P)` psi, and for uninterrupted flow. A transient excursion to `{python} dev_009_01_pmax_psi` psi in one run (DEV-009-01) lay inside the range studied. The PAR of the parameter is the whole range studied.

The step has two critical process parameters, both of the well-controlled kind. Neither parameter had a detected effect on step yield.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-control}

The step contributes two parameter ranges, a condition of operation, a test of each filter after use and its share of the modular viral clearance claim. Filtration volume is held within its NOR of `{python} rng_s(NOR_V)` L/m2 around the set-point of `{python} f"{SP_V:g}"` L/m2, and an excursion is assessed against its NOR-propagated PAR of `{python} PAR_V_N` L/m2. Filtration pressure is held within `{python} rng_s(NOR_P)` psi around `{python} f"{SP_P:g}"` psi, with a PAR of `{python} PAR_P_N` psi. The range carried into the control strategy for each parameter is the intersection of its PARs over the outputs with an adequate model (PCMP-001 §7.6). For both parameters that is the PAR for MVM LRF, because the PARs for fragments cover the range studied. Filtration is uninterrupted, because the claim does not cover an interruption of flow. An interruption at commercial scale is assessed against the mechanism of the step and not against these ranges (PCP-009 §12).

Each filter is integrity tested after use under SOP-2012. The post-use test of a parvovirus filter is designed to detect a loss of small virus retention. A membrane that passes it has no defect large enough for the test to detect. The retention of MVM depends on that integrity at least as much as the retention of XMuLV does.

The step contributes `{python} fx(CL_M)` log10 to the cumulative MVM claim, beside anion exchange (`{python} fx(CL_AEX_M)` log10, PCR-008). It contributes `{python} fx(CL_X)` log10 to the cumulative XMuLV claim, beside low-pH viral inactivation (`{python} fx(CL_VI_X)` log10, PCR-006) and anion exchange (`{python} fx(CL_AEX_X)` log10, PCR-008). Viral clearance cannot be tested on a batch, so the claim rests on the operation of the step within its ranges. Fragments are tested at release of the drug substance by nrCE-SDS against the criterion of `{python} fx(CR_F)` %, and no later step changes them. PCMR-001 consolidates these ranges, the classes and the viral clearance claims with those of the other steps.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

As the volume filtered per square metre rises, the membrane fouls and the flow shifts to the larger pores, so the MVM LRF of the step falls. The study measured this fall as a straight line from `{python} fx(M_LO)` log10 at `{python} f"{RNG_V[0]:g}"` L/m2 to `{python} fx(M_HI)` log10 at `{python} f"{RNG_V[1]:g}"` L/m2. The claim of `{python} fx(CL_M)` log10 holds on the mean prediction up to `{python} fx(CROSS_V, 1)` L/m2, `{python} fx(CROSS_MARG, 1)` L/m2 beyond the upper NOR edge of `{python} f"{NOR_V[1]:g}"` L/m2. The `{python} N_BELOW` measured MVM results below the claim were all at `{python} f"{RNG_V[1]:g}"` L/m2, beyond that point. No effect of pressure was detected on any output, and XMuLV LRF, fragments and step yield did not depend on either parameter.

The scale-down model compared step yield alone with manufacturing scale, with an offset of `{python} fx(100*OFF_Y['offset'], 1)` percentage points. No output with a criterion was compared at both scales. The clearance claims therefore rest on the spiking model, as ICH Q5A(R2) provides, and the fragment results on the mechanism of the step [@ichq5a]. The flux decay profile, which PCP-009 named as the comparison that shows whether the model fouls like the commercial filter, is not recorded (PD-009-03). How far the fouling of the scale-down membrane represents the commercial filter is therefore not shown by these data, and the effect of filtration volume on MVM LRF is the effect at scale-down.

Deleting run 5 or run 7 carries the upper PAR edge of filtration volume to the end of the range studied (@tbl-deletion). The ranges reported come from all runs and are the narrower ones. Under every deletion the edge lies `{python} f"{MARG_MIN:g}"` L/m2 or more beyond the NOR, and no deletion changed the judgement over the NOR.

The data did not show the acceleration of the MVM decline at high load, the effect of pressure or the interaction between load and pressure that the mechanism led PCP-009 to expect (@sec-mechanism). The residual SD of a model sets the standard errors of its terms. For the selected model of MVM LRF it is `{python} fx(FM['rmse'])` log10 (@tbl-adequacy), and the slope of volume is `{python} fx(T_B1, 1)` times its standard error. In the full quadratic of the planned runs the terms that PCP-009 expected have standard errors from `{python} fx(min(SE_EXP), 3)` to `{python} fx(max(SE_EXP), 3)` log10 in coded units, and none of them is significant (@tbl-appc-full). Effects of that size are not resolved by `{python} n_rsm` runs. Interruptions of flow were not studied, so the condition of uninterrupted filtration rests on the mechanism.

The record lacks several results that PCP-009 required (@sec-discrepancies). Two of them limit the claims. The record holds no spike titre and no limit of detection, so it cannot show whether any LRF is a lower bound. It also holds no integrity test result for any run, so it cannot show that each membrane was intact. The MVM results depend on that at least as much as the XMuLV results. The record names a membrane lot only in DEV-009-02, so variation between membrane lots was not studied.

The record does not name the runs of the two study events. The deletion of each response-surface run in turn covers an event that affected one of those runs. It does not cover an event that affected several runs, such as the membrane lot of DEV-009-02 (@sec-events).

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. Scale-down model (objective 1). The qualification compared step yield alone, with an offset of `{python} fx(100*OFF_Y['offset'], 1)` percentage points (`{python} f"{OFF_CI:g}"` % confidence interval `{python} fx(100*OFF_Y['lo'], 1)` to `{python} fx(100*OFF_Y['hi'], 1)`). Flux decay and the post-use integrity test are not recorded, so objective 1 was not met as PCP-009 states it. PCP-009 §7 requires this report to state what "the scale-down model is qualified" means for this step, given the outputs that the qualification compares. Only step yield was compared, and it has no criterion, so no conclusion was decided by an offset. The outputs with a criterion are judged on the scale-down results, the LRF on the spiking model and fragments on the mechanism of the step.
2. Effects (objective 2). Filtration volume lowers the mean MVM LRF by `{python} fx(-EFF_V)` log10 across `{python} rng_s(RNG_V)` L/m2. No effect of filtration pressure was detected on any output, and no effect of either parameter on XMuLV LRF, fragments or step yield.
3. Models (objective 3). The selected model of MVM LRF passes the model F-test, shows no lack of fit and meets the limit on overfitting of PCMP-001 §7.2. It fails the criterion on residuals and influential runs on run 5, the axial run at `{python} f"{RUN5.filtration_volume:g}"` L/m2 and `{python} f"{RUN5.pressure:g}"` psi. XMuLV LRF has no adequate model and is judged on its measured results. The selected models of fragments and step yield are intercept-only.
4. Proven acceptable ranges (objective 4). The NOR-propagated PAR of filtration volume is `{python} PAR_V_N` L/m2 for MVM LRF and the whole range studied for fragments. The PAR of filtration pressure is the whole range studied, `{python} PAR_P_N` psi, for both. Every PAR contains the NOR. XMuLV LRF has no adequate model and no PAR, and every measured result met its claim across the range studied.
5. Classification (objective 5). Both parameters are WC-CPP. The class of filtration pressure rests on the basis that the A-Mab case study gives and on the scope of the viral clearance claim, not on a detected effect.
6. Criteria. Each output with a criterion met its intermediate acceptance criterion across the NOR, MVM LRF at `{python} fx(M_NORHI)` log10 against `{python} fx(CL_M)`, XMuLV LRF on measured results from `{python} fx(MEAS_X.min())` log10 against `{python} fx(CL_X)`, and fragments at `{python} fx(F_PI_HI)` % against `{python} fx(CR_F)` %.
7. Design space. The design space covers `{python} fx(DS_PCT, 0)` % of the characterized region and excludes filtration volumes above `{python} fx(CROSS_V, 1)` L/m2. Deleting run 5, the run at `{python} f"{RUN5.filtration_volume:g}"` L/m2 and `{python} f"{RUN5.pressure:g}"` psi with the highest LRF at that volume, would carry the boundary to the end of the range studied.
8. Capability. The Cpk of the cumulative MVM clearance, `{python} fx(CPK_M)`, is the tightest of the attributes to which the step contributes, above the target of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` and the minimum of `{python} f"{CPK_MIN:.1f}"`. No simulated batch fell outside any criterion.
9. Success of the study. PCP-009 §7 asks for a qualified scale-down model, two viral clearance models accepted as predictive and a PAR containing the NOR for each parameter against each viral clearance response. The PARs of MVM LRF contain the NOR. The MVM model was used for prediction although it fails the criterion on residuals and influential runs (@sec-discrepancies). The XMuLV model was not accepted, so XMuLV LRF has no PAR, and its measured results met the claim across the whole range studied. The qualification compared step yield alone. The success criterion is therefore not met in full.
10. Record. Every run of the two study events was retained, as Version 1.0 recorded. The record does not name the runs, so the deletion of each run in turn covers only an event that affected a single response-surface run (@sec-events). The results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Study events and discrepancies from the plan {#sec-record}

PCP-009 calls a departure from the plan a deviation. A process characterization study is not GMP manufacture and raises no deviation. This report records the events of execution that Version 1.0 recorded as study events, under the numbers Version 1.0 gave them, and every departure from PCP-009 as a discrepancy from the plan.

## Study events {#sec-events}

Version 1.0 recorded `{python} N_EV` study events at this step (@tbl-events). It recorded that every run concerned in either event was retained in the analysis. The record does not name the runs, so no run can be analysed at its recorded conditions or excluded alone. Every run of the response-surface design was therefore deleted in turn (@tbl-deletion), and no single deletion changed the judgement over the NOR. The deletion of each run in turn covers an event that affected one response-surface run. It does not cover an event that affected several runs. Nor does it cover the screening runs, whose results enter only the screening effects and the judgement of XMuLV LRF on its measured results, or the qualification runs, which enter only the offset of step yield.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Study events of the step. {#tbl-events}")
```

### DEV-009-01, transient excursion of the filtration pressure {#sec-dev1}

During in-process pressure monitoring the filtration pressure of one run rose for a short time to a maximum of `{python} dev_009_01_pmax_psi` psi. The investigation attributed the excursion to an overshoot of the pump ramp. The record names neither the run, nor its set pressure, nor the duration of the excursion, so the run was analysed at its design setting. Version 1.0 recorded the peak as an excursion above the NOR, whose upper edge is `{python} f"{NOR_P[1]:g}"` psi. The reference for an excursion is the set pressure of the run, because the designs set runs at `{python} f"{RNG_P[0]:g}"`, `{python} f"{P_MID:g}"` and `{python} f"{RNG_P[1]:g}"` psi. An overshoot rises above the set pressure, so the run was set below `{python} dev_009_01_pmax_psi` psi, at `{python} f"{RNG_P[0]:g}"` or `{python} f"{P_MID:g}"` psi in a design or at the set-point of `{python} f"{SP_P:g}"` psi in qualification. The peak lies inside the range studied, `{python} rng_s(RNG_P)` psi, over which the designs estimated the effect of pressure, and no term containing pressure was significant for any output. If the run was a response-surface run, its deletion leaves the judgement over the NOR unchanged (@tbl-deletion). If it was a screening run, its result enters only the screening effects and the judgement of XMuLV LRF, every measured result of which met the claim. If it was a qualification run, it enters only the offset of step yield, on which no conclusion depends (@sec-sdm). The run was retained in the analysis.

### DEV-009-02, membrane lot flux below the value typical for the vendor {#sec-dev2}

The pre-use flux verification of membrane lot `{python} LOT` (`{python} LOT_VENDOR`) gave a flux `{python} dev_009_02_flux_deficit_pct` % below the value typical for the vendor. The investigation attributed the low flux to variation of membrane permeability between lots. The record names the MVM infectivity method (`{python} EV2_METHOD`) with the event, but it holds no result of an assessment by that method. Version 1.0 recorded that every run made on the lot was retained. The lot record gives the use of the lot as "`{python} LOT_USED`", and no record names the runs. The lot may therefore have been used for several runs, and the deletion of one run at a time does not bound its effect. A lower permeability lowers the flux at a given pressure. Whether it changed the retention of MVM was not tested, so the effect of the event on the results cannot be assessed from the record. The record does not link the lot to run 5.

## Discrepancies from the plan {#sec-discrepancies}

@tbl-discrepancies gives the discrepancies from PCP-009 that the register of discrepancies holds.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(discrepancy_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Discrepancies from the plan PCP-009. {#tbl-discrepancies}")
```

PD-009-01, the model selection (@sec-statistics). The full quadratic that PCP-009 planned failed the limit on overfitting for every output with a criterion (@tbl-reeval-virus-filtration). Under the plan no output with a criterion would therefore have had an adequate model. The verification of platform worst cases, from which some criteria of the campaign come, also uses the selected models. This report compared the criteria that the verification gives with the full quadratic models against the criteria in force. For this step they are the same, and so are the judgement of each output over the NOR and the PARs of MVM LRF.

PD-009-02, the MVM model used although it fails the criterion on residuals and influential runs. The PARs and the design space of MVM LRF come from the model of all runs. They are narrower than those with run 5 deleted, and no deletion changed the judgement over the NOR (@tbl-deletion).

PD-009-03, the scale-down qualification. No conclusion of this report depends on the qualification (@sec-sdm). Without the flux decay profile, whether the scale-down membrane fouls like the commercial filter is not shown, so the effect of filtration volume on MVM LRF is the effect at scale-down.

PD-009-04, the integrity tests and virus controls of the design runs. The record cannot show that each membrane was intact, on which both LRF depend, or whether any LRF is a lower bound (@sec-analytical). No run was excluded for a failed integrity test, because no test result is recorded.

PD-009-05, step yield and filtrate fractions. The record names no method for the step yield (@sec-operation). Without fractions the effect of filtration volume on MVM LRF is estimated between runs only (@sec-sampling).

PD-009-06, the load material and the flux of the spiked runs. Whether the spiked load fouled the membrane differently from unspiked process material is not shown. PCP-009 §12 named that bias as largest at the top of the volume range, on which the claim depends.

PD-009-07, analyses the plan does not contain. They are the analyses that @sec-statistics lists as not in PCP-009. Of the PAR figures that the plan asked for, only @fig-par-mvm is given.

# Appendix C. Full effect and coefficient tables {.unnumbered #sec-appC}

@tbl-appc-scr gives every effect of the screening models with its coefficient, @tbl-appc-sel the coefficients of every selected model of the response-surface design, and @tbl-appc-full the coefficients of the full quadratic models that PCP-009 planned, which Version 1.0 used.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows_appc_scr = []
for _r in RESP4:
    _sc = 100 if _r == "step_yield" else 1
    for _t in ["A", "B", "AB"]:
        _e = SE[_r].loc[_t]
        _rows_appc_scr.append([f"{_lab2[_r]} ({_unit[_r]})", _t, fx(_e["Effect"] * _sc, 3), fx(_e["Coef."] * _sc, 3),
                      fx(_e["Std. err."] * _sc, 3), fx(_e["t"], 2), pn(_e["p-value"])])
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_rows_appc_scr, columns=["Response", "Term", "Effect", "Coefficient", "Std. err.", "t", "p-value"]),
        "Effects and coefficients of the screening models.", "tbl-appc-scr", merge=["Response"],
        align=["l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "A, filtration volume. B, filtration pressure. AB, their interaction. Coefficients in coded units. "
                    "Std. err., the standard error of the coefficient.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```
